title: Section 98 — Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.

content.overview: BNS s. 98 — Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc. BNS restatement of IPC 372. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 372. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 98 is the rule on “Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc”. The section provides that whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 98 exists so that “Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
98. Whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Explanations
Explanation 1.—When a female under the age of eighteen years is sold, let for hire, or otherwise disposed of to a prostitute or to any person who keeps or manages a brothel, the person so disposing of such female shall, until the contrary is proved, be presumed to have disposed of her with the intent that she shall be used for the purpose of prostitution

Explanation 2.—For the purposes of this section “illicit intercourse” means sexual intercourse between persons not united by marriage or by any union or tie which, though not amounting to a marriage, is recognised by the personal law or custom of the community to which they belong or, where they belong to different communities, of both such communities, as constituting between them a quasi-marital relation

learningObjectives: Master the offence of selling, letting to hire, or disposing of a child for prostitution or unlawful/immoral purposes under BNS s. 98.
Understand the statutory presumption under Explanation 1 regarding disposal of a female under eighteen to a brothel keeper or prostitute.
Analyze the definition of illicit intercourse under Explanation 2 and the ten-year imprisonment tier.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 98 provides that whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Prohibits the commercial trafficking and disposal of children for sexual exploitation, reversing the burden of proof when a minor is transferred to brothel managers or prostitutes.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 98 (corresponding to IPC s. 372).
Actus reus: Selling, letting to hire, or otherwise disposing of any child (under eighteen years).
Mens rea: Intent or knowledge that the child will at any age be employed or used for prostitution, illicit intercourse, or any unlawful and immoral purpose.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to ten years, and fine.
Explanation 1: Presumption of intent for prostitution when a female under eighteen is sold, hired, or disposed of to a prostitute or brothel keeper.
Explanation 2: Defines 'illicit intercourse' as sexual intercourse between persons not united by marriage or recognized quasi-marital union.
essentialIngredients: The person sold or disposed of is a child (under eighteen years of age).
The accused sold, let to hire, or otherwise disposed of the child.
The act was done with intent, or knowing it to be likely, that the child would at any age be used for prostitution, illicit intercourse, or any unlawful and immoral purpose.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 98 is a core penal shield against child trafficking. It targets the seller or disposer of a child under eighteen years of age. The modes of transfer include selling, letting on hire, or 'otherwise disposing of' (a broad residuary phrase covering gifts, pledges, or transfers of custody). The contemplated exploitation does not need to be immediate: the statutory phrase 'shall at any age be employed or used' means selling an infant or young child with the intent that they be exploited upon reaching adolescence is fully punishable. Explanation 1 introduces an evidentiary presumption: disposing of a female minor to a known prostitute or brothel keeper creates a legal presumption of trafficking intent. Explanation 2 defines illicit intercourse as sexual relations outside a valid marriage or recognized quasi-marital tie.
examples: Teaching example (Selling a minor to a brothel): A guardian sells custody of a fourteen-year-old girl to a brothel owner for a sum of money. Under Explanation 1, the law presumes the disposal was for the purpose of prostitution. The guardian is guilty under s. 98.

Teaching example (Future exploitation intent): A person transfers custody of a ten-year-old child to a commercial syndicate with the agreement that the child will be trained for commercial sexual exploitation upon turning fourteen. This satisfies s. 98 ('at any age').
distinctions: Section 98 vs Section 99: Section 98 penalizes the seller/disposer (the supply side); Section 99 penalizes the buyer/receiver (the demand side).
Section 98 vs Section 96: Section 96 punishes inducing a child to go for illicit intercourse; Section 98 punishes commercial transactions of selling, hiring, or disposing of possession.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a person who transferred custody of a sixteen-year-old girl to a brothel operator for a monthly rental payment can argue that no sexual acts had yet occurred.
Rule: Under BNS s. 98, letting to hire with intent or knowledge of future prostitution completes the offence; actual sexual acts are not required, and Explanation 1 presumes intent.
Application: Letting for hire to a brothel operator triggers the statutory presumption of intent.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 98.

keyTakeaways: Penalizes selling, hiring, or disposing of a child under eighteen.
Exploitation can be intended 'at any age' (immediate or future).
Explanation 1 establishes a statutory presumption against brothel transfers.
Punishable with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
